"It was building over the last five days when he was trying to throw a bullpen, go through a throwing program," said manager Torey Lovullo of Burnes' injury. "It just wasn't working and he couldn't figure out why." Arizona is expected to go with a bullpen game, with Jose Cabrera (0-3, 4.33 ERA) a possibility to get bulk innings or even start. Ryne Nelson and Zac Gallen were mentioned as candidates before Friday's game but both closed out Brandon Pfaadt's third win over the Padres. Catcher Gabriel Moreno (left hamstring) left Friday's game early but is expected to serve as the designated hitter on Saturday night. Meanwhile, San Diego (89-71) also won despite losing. With the Chicago Cubs being swept in Boston and the Phillies' shutout loss, the Padres need just one win in the last two games to earn home-field advantage for the NL wild-card round. San Diego manager Craig Stammen said that Friday's loss doesn't make his decisions for the rest of the weekend any more complicated. "We have to go out and play a baseball game," he said. "Getting blown out, we were able to get some of these guys off their feet a little bit. I would anticipate getting those guys back in the lineup tomorrow." Stammen cleared the bench when his team trailed 10-2 after six innings, giving mainstays such as Jackson Merrill, Fernando Tatis Jr. and Xander Bogaerts the final three innings off. The Padres will turn to Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56) on Saturday. He enjoyed one of his best outings of the year Sunday in a 7-3 win over Miami, lasting 6 2/3 innings and allowing three runs off three hits and two walks with six strikeouts. Buehler is 7-1 with a 2.57 ERA in 16 career outings (15 starts) against Arizona, with the one loss coming on July 6. That day, he allowed seven runs on seven hits in five innings in an 8-0 loss. --Field Level Media

item.title: Braves strive to get past Marlins on way to playoffs
item.description: The Atlanta Braves, who will visit the Miami Marlins on Saturday afternoon in the teams' next-to-last game of the regular season, are facing issues concerning their rotation.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves, who will visit the Miami Marlins on Saturday afternoon in the teams' next-to-last game of the regular season, are facing issues concerning their rotation. Left-hander Martin Perez (lower back inflammation) is on the injured list and likely will miss the first two rounds of the playoffs for the National League East champion Braves (93-67). Losing Perez (9-9, 3.04 ERA) is a blow for Atlanta. Chris Sale (14-9, 2.16 ERA) is the Braves' ace, and Grant Holmes (10-6, 3.44 ERA) is set for the postseason rotation, too. The Braves also feel good about Tyler Mahle, who was acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the trade deadline last month. Mahle went 3-9 (5.13 ERA) with the Giants but is 4-1 with a 1.99 ERA for the Braves. After that, the Braves start to dim in the rotation, with converted reliever JR Ritchie (1-4, 4.79 ERA) likely next in line. The Braves have had an excellent season, winning their seventh division title over the past nine years. But the lack of rotation depth -- especially with Bryce Elder (8-8, 4.11 ERA) also on the injured list -- could plague their playoff push. However, Braves manager Walt Weiss has another view, at least publicly. "It's business as usual," he told mlb.com. "The way things have gone this year, somebody's probably going to get a bigger opportunity and make something of it." Meanwhile, the Marlins (79-81) are putting the finishing touches on another disappointing season. They have not made the playoffs since 2023 and were officially eliminated from playoff contention last week. "We put our players first from a health standpoint," manager Clayton McCullough said Friday. "But, outside of that, we will try to win as many games as possible this weekend, especially at home, where we've had a successful year." The Marlins, who are 46-33 at home this season, made news this week as shortstop Otto Lopez was named Miami's 2026 Roberto Clemente Award nominee. The award goes to the player who, as MLB.com describes it, "best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy, and positive contributions, both on and off the field." Mookie Betts of the Dodgers won the 2025 Clemente Award. On Saturday, the Marlins likely will face a Braves bullpen game, according to Weiss. The Braves will send left-hander Brent Suter (3-2, 3.48 ERA) to the mound first. Suter got the win in relief his last time out, pitching a scoreless top of the 10th on Wednesday before the Braves walked off Cincinnati 3-2 in the bottom of the inning. Suter is 2-1 with an ERA of 4.37 in 11 career appearances against the Marlins. "The priority is getting guys appearances and also getting them their rest," Weiss said of his pitchers. "We want to maintain some momentum going into the postseason. We're trying to find a sweet spot between being rested and being ready to go (for the playoffs). "Position-player-wise, we're just going to continue to play as usual." Jack Ralston (0-2, 4.50 ERA) will start for Miami on Saturday. The right-hander took the loss in his last outing, allowing two runs on three hits in 1 1/3 innings in a 2-1 defeat to the Chicago Cubs on Thursday. He has never faced the Braves. --Field Level Media

item.title: ANÁLISIS Presidenta encargada de Venezuela vuelve de EEUU sin acuerdos ni fecha para elecciones
item.description: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, llegó esta semana a Nueva York para la Asamblea General de la ONU en busca de acuerdos comerciales en materia de deuda, energía y minería, para mostrar que el país, que alguna vez estuvo bajo fuertes sanciones, está otra vez abierto a los negocios tras la captura de su predecesor por parte de fuerzas estadounidenses.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, llegó esta semana a Nueva York para la Asamblea General de la ONU en busca de [USN:L6N45E138 TEXT:"acuerdos"] comerciales en materia de deuda, energía y minería, para mostrar que el país, que alguna vez estuvo bajo fuertes sanciones, está otra vez abierto a los negocios tras la captura de su predecesor por parte de fuerzas estadounidenses. En su discurso ante la ONU, prometió que el país sudamericano miembro de la OPEP [USN:S0N3ST09E TEXT:"celebraría elecciones"] como parte de una transición hacia la "democracia plena". Se marchó con fotografías suyas junto al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pero no obtuvo ningún acuerdo concreto. Fue su primera visita a Estados Unidos desde la salida del entonces presidente Nicolás Maduro tras una redada en enero. Y con ella quedó en evidencia el profundo control que Washington ejerce sobre su Gobierno y la necesidad de Venezuela de forjar nuevas alianzas para alinearse con las aspiraciones de Trump, dijeron analistas. "Rodríguez tuvo una semana de alta exposición. Pero cuando hacemos el inventario de resultados concretos anunciados, el balance es modesto. ¿Dónde están los desembolsos?, ¿el paquete de reconstrucción?, ¿los grandes acuerdos empresariales? No se materializaron en la magnitud que habría permitido presentar Nueva York como el gran regreso financiero de Venezuela", dijo el analista basado en Washington Antonio De La Cruz. "Al vencedor le pertenecen los despojos", dijo Trump ante la asamblea el martes, mientras Rodríguez escuchaba. Le recordó que Estados Unidos estuvo listo para usar su "poder militar sin igual". En su discurso, Trump no mencionó a Rodríguez y tampoco se publicó la transcripción de su breve conversación con ella. Líderes de izquierda de otros países que antes apoyaban a Maduro mantuvieron distancia, mientras que venezolanos residentes en Estados Unidos protestaron frente a la ONU con pancartas que mostraban a Rodríguez con el uniforme naranja que es tradicional en muchas cárceles. Según De La Cruz, Trump demostró que Washington está moldeando el nuevo panorama venezolano, mientras que Rodríguez se mostró como la interlocutora clave. "Pero ella carga ahora con una consecuencia adicional: tendrá que explicar cuándo votarán los venezolanos". Durante nueve meses, Rodríguez evitó dar señales sobre la celebración de elecciones, mientras que funcionarios estadounidenses mantuvieron las expectativas a raya al afirmar que su concreción llevaría tiempo. Analistas y partidos de la oposición venezolana ahora señalan que el tiempo corre para fijar una fecha, mientras expertos estiman que se necesitarán al menos 12 meses para nombrar autoridades confiables y organizar la votación. La Casa Blanca y los ministerios de Información y de Relaciones Exteriores de Venezuela no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios sobre una posible elección y los detalles de las conversaciones bilaterales. MUCHO RUIDO, NINGÚN ACUERDO Se [USN:L1N45D0KY TEXT:"esperaba"] que las conversaciones con funcionarios estadounidenses, organismos multilaterales, gobiernos aliados y empresas energéticas y mineras dieran como resultado la firma de acuerdos, aunque fueran preliminares, dijeron fuentes antes del viaje de la delegación venezolana. Hasta el sábado, no se había anunciado ninguno. El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID), Ilan Goldfajn, dijo que la institución multilateral está trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo puente de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela. Sin embargo, algunos miembros del consejo del BID se oponen a la concesión del préstamo, informó Reuters el martes. Puertas adentro en la ONU, los venezolanos se encontraban prácticamente solos. La delegación cubana, otrora el aliado más cercano de la nación sudamericana, abandonó la sala cuando el discurso de Trump se centró en Cuba, mientras que Rodríguez permaneció en la sala cuando el mandatario estadounidense calificó a Maduro de "dictador fuera de la ley". Según fuentes, funcionarios de Caracas y La Habana evitaron el contacto entre sí. Cuando Rodríguez cruzó el hemiciclo para hablar con el jefe del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, él terminó torpemente una llamada telefónica antes de ponerse de pie para saludarla. Sánchez describió posteriormente el saludo como "normal". Mientras tanto, una fuente dijo a Reuters que la delegación rusa solicitó una reunión con el canciller venezolano, Félix Plasencia, para discutir los intereses del país en proyectos petroleros en Venezuela. La solicitud se hizo mientras circulan [USN:L6N458178 TEXT:"informes"] de que ExxonMobil (XOM.N) ha mantenido negociaciones para regresar al proyecto Petromonagas, propiedad en parte de la empresa estatal rusa Roszarubezhneft. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia, su misión ante la ONU en Nueva York y su embajada en Caracas no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. El presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, el líder izquierdista más destacado de la región, dijo a CNN que Estados Unidos trata a Rodríguez como si fuera su jefe y que, en su lugar, él convocaría elecciones. Fuera de la sede de la ONU, más de 50 manifestantes portaron pancartas con el lema "Nueva cara, mismo régimen" y corearon que Rodríguez debería unirse a Maduro en la cárcel de Brooklyn donde se encuentra detenido a la espera de juicio. Tras la reunión de Rodríguez con Trump, el secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, dijo que ambos abordaron la reestructuración de la deuda soberana de Venezuela y que Washington presionó por un cambio político, dos temas difíciles para la administración interina. "Para que este proyecto tenga éxito, debe culminar en unas elecciones libres y justas", dijo Rubio. Mientras Rodríguez visitaba Estados Unidos, medios de comunicación informaron que a la líder de la oposición venezolana, María Corina Machado, quien podría ser una candidata fuerte en unas eventuales elecciones, se le impidió nuevamente regresar a su país desde Panamá. Nicmer Evans, analista político y antiguo partidario del fallecido presidente izquierdista Hugo Chávez, teorizó en X que Rodríguez se había dejado "humillar doblemente" a cambio de que Trump le negara su apoyo a Machado. "Habrá elecciones, pero cuando Estados Unidos lo considere", dijo Evans.

item.title: India's election commission orders review of voter-roll changes
item.description: The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters. Opposition parties have said the lists have been manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission of India has said differences are normal in any institution, and that all its actions were lawful. The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating voters' lists that began last year. Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have [USN:L1N45H06Y TEXT:"demanded Kumar's resignation"]. The CJP said it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if he did not quit by Saturday. The Commission said on Saturday that a committee led by a senior election official and including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules. It also said local officials would visit voters flagged for discrepancies instead of routinely requiring them to appear at government offices.

item.title: Blue Jays seek to take series from Reds, end season on positive note
item.description: Third baseman Kazuma Okamoto has been a bright spot for the Toronto Blue Jays in their disappointing season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Third baseman Kazuma Okamoto has been a bright spot for the Toronto Blue Jays in their disappointing season. He had two doubles and three RBIs on Friday night in a 6-5 victory over the visiting Cincinnati Reds (74-86) in the opener of a three-game series, with Game 2 on tap for Saturday afternoon. Okamoto leads the Blue Jays (78-82) with 92 RBIs and has put them in a position to end their season with a series win. He also has 33 home runs in his first season in the majors after leaving Japan. "He's been fantastic," Toronto manager John Schneider said. "He's just preparing, adjusting and showing off the hitter that he is." The Blue Jays will start right-hander Trey Yesavage (5-5, 3.67 ERA) on Saturday in an attempt to clinch the series. He has never faced the Reds. Cincinnati is slated to start right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12, 6.01), who has not opposed the Blue Jays. One of the biggest disappointments for Toronto has been the lack of hitting by Vladimir Guerrero Jr., who is in the first season of a $500 million, 14-year contract and has only nine home runs. Before Friday's game, he took advantage of a second chance to walk back comments he made on a podcast that caused an uproar. "The main reason I'm here is because I regret my comments I made the other day, " Guerrero said through translator Hector Lebron. "I feel from my heart that my fans, my teammates, they need an apology from me, and that's (what) I'm here for." In an interview in Spanish with Veronica Batista of Noticias Telemicro on Wednesday, Guerrero said: "The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 (home runs) every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished.' When asked in Baltimore after the Jays were eliminated from playoff contention with a 4-2 loss in the opening game of a doubleheader on Wednesday, he stood by what he had said. He apparently changed his mind about an apology on the off-day Thursday and addressed a media scrum on Friday. The fan reaction during Friday's game was mild and mixed. Guerrero went 1-for-5 with a broken-bat RBI single, giving him 57 RBIs for the season. The positive occurrence for the Reds on Friday came when Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run double in the third inning and stole third base on the next pitch. He became the fourth player in Reds' history to have at least 30 home runs and 30 stolen bases in the same season. The double also was his 30th. "It's really special," De La Cruz said. "That means a great season. I know as a group this season didn't go the way we wanted it to. But it's a great season individually." The other Cincinnati players with 30 homers and 30 steals in a season were Brandon Phillips (2007), Barry Larkin (1996), and Eric Davis (1987). "Those are great guys. They play hard. They play the game the right way," De La Cruz, 24, said. "It's really good to join them." "He's still really young. He's still developing. He's getting better," Reds bench coach Mike Napoli said. "He's hungry to get better. You would expect him to be that superstar. He's gotten better every single year. We expect him to get better." --Field Level Media

item.title: Munich picked as Germany’s candidate to host Summer Games
item.description: Munich has been chosen as Germany's city to bid to host the Summer Olympic Games in 2036, 2040 or 2044, the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) voted on Saturday, as the country launched its latest attempt to land the world's biggest multi-sport event for the first time since 1972.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Munich has been chosen as Germany's city to bid to host the Summer Olympic Games in 2036, 2040 or 2044, the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) voted on Saturday, as the country launched its latest attempt to land the world's biggest multi-sport event for the first time since 1972. Munich, the last German summer Games host 54 years ago, was one of originally three candidate cities for the vote, along with Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr and Berlin, but the capital pulled the plug two days before the vote following local elections last week. "The winner is Munich," German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said at the DOSB general assembly after being handed the envelope with the winning bid. "If we go to the starting line as Team Germany then we have good chance to become Olympic hosts," he had earlier said. Munich's bid, which includes use of the Olympic park built for the 1972 Games, enjoys strong local support. It will face stiff competition, especially for 2036, with the IOC having said more than 10 cities or countries had expressed an interest, among them Indonesia, India, South Africa, Chile's Santiago as well as Doha, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. Los Angeles will host the 2028 Olympics and Brisbane, Australia will stage the 2032 edition. There is no date for a decision by the International Olympic Committee which has changed its bidding rules in recent years, with several stages of dialogues with interested parties resulting in one preferred candidate to be put to the vote. The IOC usually awards the Games about seven years in advance. Germany last hosted the Summer Olympics in 1972 in the Bavarian capital, which were marred when Palestinians from the Black September militant group took members of the Israeli Olympic team hostage. Eleven Israelis, a German policeman and five of the Palestinian gunmen died after a stand-off at the Olympic village and the nearby Fuerstenfeldbruck airfield. Previous efforts by Germany to land Summer or Winter Games failed mostly at the first hurdle with local referendums opposing such plans over their size and cost, as was the case for Hamburg which was planning a bid for 2024. Munich had also unsuccessfully bid for the 2018 Olympics, finishing second behind Pyeongchang in South Korea.

item.title: Huracán Polo, de categoría 5, amenaza la costa de México; se prevé que toque tierra el lunes
item.description: El huracán Polo se alejaba el sábado de la costa del Pacífico mexicano tras recuperar la máxima intensidad de categoría 5, antes de que se previera su regreso para tocar tierra en Baja California Sur el lunes, según los meteorólogos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Polo se alejaba el sábado de la costa del Pacífico mexicano tras recuperar la máxima intensidad de categoría 5, antes de que se previera su regreso para tocar tierra en Baja California Sur el lunes, según los meteorólogos. Polo se encontraba el sábado por la mañana a unas 425 millas (684 kilómetros) al suroeste de la localidad turística mexicana de Cabo Corrientes, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 160 millas por hora (257 kilómetros), según el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC) de Estados Unidos. La tormenta se desplazaba hacia el noroeste a 10 millas por hora (16 kilómetros). AccuWeather, un servicio meteorológico privado, informó que, 24 horas después de impactar en Baja California, se esperaba que el huracán tocara tierra por segunda vez en la costa continental del noroeste de México, provocando posibles inundaciones repentinas peligrosas para la vida en partes de Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Sonora y Chihuahua. Las fuertes lluvias y los vientos intensos del huracán a lo largo de la costa del Pacífico mexicano obligaron a realizar evacuaciones, cerrar puertos y suspender clases esta semana. En la ciudad turística de San José del Cabo, la policía restringió el acceso a una playa el viernes debido a que el huracán generaba olas altas y condiciones de oleaje peligroso. Es posible que se registren condiciones de huracán el lunes por la tarde desde Punta Eugenia hasta Santa Fe, en Baja California, señaló el NHC. Se prevé que Polo deje entre 4 y 8 pulgadas de lluvia en partes de Baja California Sur, con acumulaciones máximas de 10 pulgadas, lo que podría provocar inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que pongan en peligro vidas humanas, indicó el NHC. Asimismo, podría generar oleaje peligroso, corrientes de resaca e inundaciones costeras.

item.title: León al frente del mayor acto celebrado en Francia, mientras las multitudes esperan un mensaje de paz
item.description: Una multitud se congregaba el sábado en la Avenida de los Campos Elíseos de París, a la espera de la llegada del papa León para una misa al aire libre que se preveía que fuera el acto más importante de su visita de fin de semana a Francia.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee, Elizabeth Pineau
item.content:encoded: Una multitud se congregaba el sábado en la Avenida de los Campos Elíseos de París, a la espera de la llegada del papa León para una misa al aire libre que se preveía que fuera el acto más importante de su visita de fin de semana a Francia. Más de 600.000 personas se inscribieron para asistir a la misa de media tarde, y las multitudes comenzaron a llegar antes del amanecer, agolpándose frente a las vallas que bordeaban el bulevar arbolado y ondeando banderas blancas y amarillas del Vaticano. En las inmediaciones, la policía cerró las calles por las que León pasaría en un papamóvil descapotable. Geraldine Pambou, de 42 años, dijo que esperaba que León, quien este año fue reprendido por el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, por criticar la guerra contra Irán, volviera a alzar la voz en favor de la paz. "Lo más importante es que haga hincapié en la paz mundial", afirmó. "Hay demasiadas guerras". León está en una visita de cuatro días por tres ciudades de Francia, donde busca restaurar la reputación de la Iglesia tras los escándalos de abusos que causaron conmoción en todo el país. El papa, que ha condenado enérgicamente la dirección que han tomado los líderes mundiales en los últimos meses, advirtió el viernes, en un discurso pronunciado en la sede parisina de la UNESCO, el organismo de la ONU para la cultura y la educación, que la ONU y otros organismos multilaterales se encontraban en crisis. También reiteró su frecuente llamado para que el mundo reconsidere el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, y señaló a los líderes franceses que la IA podría crear un futuro en el que "un paraíso de máquinas" tomara el control de la Tierra. Pierre-Marie Estienne, de 36 años, estaba entre la multitud que esperaba la misa de León en el centro de París junto a su esposa y sus cuatro hijos pequeños. "Vivimos en una época de gran materialismo", afirmó. "Hay mucho mal a nuestro alrededor, por lo que necesitamos un mensaje de esperanza y amor". EL PAPA VISITA A LOS CATÓLICOS RECIÉN BAUTIZADOS Francia, una nación laica en la que la separación entre Iglesia y Estado está consagrada en una ley de 1905, ha sido testigo de un descenso constante de la afiliación a la Iglesia católica desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial, lo que refleja una tendencia observada en otros países tradicionalmente católicos. Aunque la Conferencia Episcopal Francesa señala un aumento de los bautismos de adultos —incluido un récord de 21.000 la pasada Semana Santa—, un reporte publicado por la agencia oficial de estadísticas, el INSEE, reveló que solo el 25% de los franceses de entre 18 y 49 años se identificaban como católicos, frente al 43% de una década antes. En una visita el sábado a los católicos recién bautizados en la Universidad Católica de París, León instó a la Iglesia francesa a no mostrarse "ingenuamente optimista" respecto al reciente aumento de fieles. "Debemos reconocer, acoger y proteger la pequeña llama que el Espíritu Santo ha encendido en la oscuridad de la noche, la diminuta semilla que se esfuerza por crecer incluso entre las espinas", afirmó. León se desplazará más tarde este sábado a Lourdes, sede de un santuario católico. Allí se reunirá el domingo con siete víctimas francesas de abusos por parte del clero.

item.title: Monzo negocia su venta a Nubank por valoración de unos 10.000 millones de libras: Sky News
item.description: El banco brasileño Nubank está en una fase inicial de negociaciones con el banco digital británico Monzo sobre una posible fusión que podría valorar a Monzo entre 8.000 y 10.000 millones de libras esterlinas (entre 10.600 y 13.250 millones de dólares), según informó Sky News el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El banco brasileño Nubank (NU.N) está en una fase inicial de negociaciones con el banco digital británico Monzo sobre una posible fusión que podría valorar a Monzo entre 8.000 y 10.000 millones de libras esterlinas (entre 10.600 y 13.250 millones de dólares), según informó Sky News el sábado. La adquisición por parte de Nubank es una de las dos opciones que el consejo de administración de Monzo está barajando actualmente, según Sky News, que cita a una fuente cercana al proceso. La otra opción es una nueva ronda de financiamiento que se espera que valore a Monzo en más de 8.000 millones de libras, cuyos ingresos se destinarían a una expansión en Europa continental, según el informe. Monzo se ha negado a hacer comentarios. No ha sido posible contactar con Nubank para recabar sus comentarios fuera del horario laboral habitual. Nubank, con sede en São Paulo, cotiza en la Bolsa de Nueva York con una capitalización bursátil de unos 65.500 millones de dólares. Monzo, con sede en Londres, obtuvo un beneficio antes de impuestos de 87,3 millones de libras esterlinas en el ejercicio cerrado a 31 de marzo, frente a los 60,5 millones del año anterior, mientras que los ingresos crecieron de 1.200 millones a 1.700 millones de libras esterlinas, según su informe anual. El pasado mes de octubre, Monzo fue valorada en 4.500 millones de libras esterlinas en una venta de acciones de los empleados a inversores, entre los que se encontraban el fondo soberano de Singapur GIC y StepStone Group. (1 dólar = 0,7547 libras)

item.title: Gold Fields expresses interest in buying Northern Star, Bloomberg reports
item.description: South African miner Gold Fields has expressed interest in buying Australia's largest gold miner Northern Star , Bloomberg News reported on Saturday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South African miner Gold Fields (GFIJ.J) has expressed interest in buying Australia's largest gold miner Northern Star (NST.AX) , Bloomberg News reported on Saturday, citing people with knowledge of the matter. Here are further details: Gold Fields recently approached Northern Star about a transaction, Bloomberg said. However, the Australian miner rebuffed the overtures, and Gold Fields is considering its next steps, Bloomberg said. Gold Fields and Northern Star did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours.

item.title: Rangers determined to stay positive in rematch vs. Twins
item.description: The Texas Rangers have no time to dwell on their latest setback.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers have no time to dwell on their latest setback. They still are tied with the Houston Astros for first place in the American League West. They still have a shot at reaching the postseason if they finish one game ahead of their in-state rivals. Texas (79-81) will look to keep its postseason hopes alive when it squares off against the Minnesota Twins (76-84) on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. The Twins won the series opener 10-2, but the Rangers are determined to stay positive going forward. "We have to," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said. "That's the only way to do it. Two games left. "... The important thing is to come back (Saturday) and do whatever we can to fight and to try to win that game. That's the most important game. Tough one (Friday), no doubt about it, but we have to figure out a way to keep going and stay positive and win." Texas will need to do so without Josh Jung, who broke a bone in his hand after he was hit by a pitch Friday. Jung appeared in 104 games in a season interrupted by injuries. Rangers right-hander Nathan Eovaldi (11-10, 4.27 ERA) is expected to take the mound on Saturday. He has 141 strikeouts in 141 1/3 innings this season and has appeared in 26 games, including 22 starts. Eovaldi has not started a game since Aug. 7 against the Baltimore Orioles. He is searching for his first victory since July 25 against the Seattle Mariners. In nine career starts against Minnesota, Eovaldi is 4-4 with a 4.75 ERA. This will be his first appearance against the Twins since 2024, when he allowed four runs (three earned) on six hits in seven innings and took the loss for the Rangers. Twins right-hander Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.21) is set to make his 24th and final start of the season. He needs five more strikeouts to reach 700 for his career. Ober is back in the rotation after serving a brief stint in the bullpen. In his last outing, he earned his first career save by pitching three scoreless innings to close out a victory over the Los Angeles Angels. This will be Ober's sixth career start against Texas. He is 2-1 with a 5.61 ERA in his first five outings, and he has walked 14 and struck out 20 in 25 2/3 innings. Ober has played his entire career for Minnesota. He has one year left on his contract, but he knows that change is possible during the offseason. "I feel like there's always going to be options," Ober said. "Especially when we have eight starters. Guys like me, Joe (Ryan), Pablo (Lopez) and Dean (Kremer) will all be free agents the same year. And then you have a lot of young guys that have a lot of potential behind us. "So there's always going to be chatter and thoughts. You never know if you're going to get moved. ... Obviously I'd love to stay here. But you never know. It's kind of up to the bigwigs up top to decide that." -Field Level Media

item.title: Russell fends off Verstappen to win in Baku, Antonelli fifth
item.description: The win closes the gap to Russell's teammate and championship leader, Antonelli, by 15 points, to 66.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Takle
item.content:encoded: George Russell closed the gap to championship-leading Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the Formula One standings after fending off Red Bull’s Max Verstappen to complete a lights-to-flag win in Saturday’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the Italian fifth. Russell took the flag just 0.196 seconds ahead of the flying Dutchman, who had started eighth but crossed the line nearly side-by-side with his Mercedes rival, after two safety car phases turned a Saturday cruise into a fight for survival for the Briton. Frenchman Isack Hadjar completed a double podium for Red Bull, repaying the team’s decision to give him a contract extension with third on his return to racing action. “It’s amazing to be back on the top step of the podium,” said Russell, after closing the gap to Antonelli from 81 to 66 points in the overall standings with 15 races completed. “Every race since the (summer) break I have gone from strength to strength and I feel more like myself again.” RUSSELL'S FIRST WIN SINCE JUNE Antonelli had started 16th after a rare error saw him crash out of Friday’s qualifying. His drive on Saturday was less like his Monza charge – where he went from 19th to first – and more a slow-burn recovery. Saturday’s win was the eighth of Russell’s career, his third of the season and first since the Austrian Grand Prix in June. It capped a dominant weekend for the Briton and had seemed a mere formality, with the 28-year-old leading off the line and opening up a comfortable lead ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar. But all that changed on the 31st of the race’s 51 laps when a crash for Williams racer Alex Albon brought out the safety car. Russell’s 11-second lead evaporated as the safety car bunched up the field. Verstappen snatched second from Piastri into the first corner as the action resumed, with Russell unchallenged. But the race was neutralised almost instantly by another safety car when Argentine Franco Colapinto locked up and ploughed into Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, who in turn collected McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris. Colapinto, who was given a 10-second time penalty, continued but the contact put both Gasly and Norris out of the race. The fuming Briton called for the 23-year-old Colapinto to be banned. Russell had Verstappen right on his tail at the second restart. The Mercedes driver kept the lead but was unable to shake off the chasing Red Bull, with the pair trading fastest laps. It looked like the Dutchman, brushing the barriers as he hunted down his first win of the season, might just snatch victory on the final dash to the line but the Briton doggedly clung on. “We had a good race, a tricky first stint on the mediums (tyres) but we got a good restart,” said Verstappen. “Then the final lap George lost boost and I got close, but it was not enough.” Behind them, Hadjar inherited third when Piastri locked up and took to the run-off area. The Australian, who had started third, dropped to 14th compounding a miserable day for McLaren. “It has been a very long six weeks since I injured myself,” said Hadjar, who missed the last three races with a wrist injury. “It was the right time to come back, I felt strong, I took it step by step to gain the confidence,” added the 21-year-old who was also on the podium in Monaco. Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari. His seven-times world champion teammate Lewis Hamilton was sixth. Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad was seventh while Esteban Ocon took eighth ahead of teammate Oliver Bearman in a double points finish for Haas. Carlos Sainz rounded out the top 10 for Williams.

item.title: Markram hopes Australia get a respectful reception in test series
item.description: South Africa batter Aiden Markram admits he does not know what sort of reception the Australian team will get from the home crowds in next month’s three-match test series, but hopes it is a respectful one.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa batter Aiden Markram admits he does not know what sort of reception the Australian team will get from the home crowds in next month’s three-match test series, but hopes it is a respectful one. The matches in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town are the first time the teams meet in tests in South Africa since the infamous 2018 "Sandpapergate" scandal where the tourists were guilty of trying to alter the condition of the ball in the third test at Newlands in Cape Town. The fallout led to lengthy bans for Australia captain Steve Smith, and batters David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, and a review of the conduct of the Australian team. The memory of the incident could add extra spice to a series that is never short of an edge, with South Africa having defeated Australia in the World Test Championship final last year. "I’ve got no idea what it’s (fan reception) going to be like," Markram told reporters on Saturday. "Obviously, 2018 was a long time ago, and there will be fans who probably haven’t forgotten what happened. "But there will also be quite a few who have moved on and understand that things look very different now (in the Australia team). "We’re certainly not encouraging anything disrespectful, but you hope the crowd really gets into the game and enjoys watching good cricket." NEW RELATIONSHIPS Markram says the proliferation of Twenty20 leagues has seen adversaries become teammates and helped develop relationships off the pitch. "I’ve spent quite a bit of time with Mitch (Marsh) during the last IPL (Indian Premier League) and with some of the other Australian players here and there as well. That’s what franchise cricket does. "But I think when you cross the boundary, you forget about all of that. It becomes a battle between two teams who are pushing really hard to get results and win games of cricket." South Africa lead the current three-match one-day international series 1-0 heading into the second game in Johannesburg on Sunday. Markram believes it is a good test for both teams ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup that will be co-hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe. "You naturally want to measure your own team and understand where you are. You want to know how you can keep building and make sure you go into the next World Cup with plenty of energy," he said.

item.title: For White Sox, work remains against Rockies
item.description: With a spot in the American League playoffs assured but seeding still to be determined, the Chicago White Sox realize they only can concern themselves with what they can control.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With a spot in the American League playoffs assured but seeding still to be determined, the Chicago White Sox realize they only can concern themselves with what they can control. Wins in five of the past six games entering Saturday night's visit from the Colorado Rockies show that Chicago is surging as the regular season concludes. Right now, that's enough. "Just looking to keep this continuing for the next two days and roll into October," White Sox right-hander Sean Burke said. Burke pitched 5 1/3 innings of one-run ball and Munetaka Murakami had two solo home runs among his three hits and three RBIs to spark the White Sox to a 6-1 victory against Colorado in Friday's series opener. Chicago (83-77) remains one game behind the AL Central-leading Guardians after Cleveland's 12-9 win in Kansas City on Friday. The White Sox hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Guardians. One of the teams will win the division; the other will head to the AL wild-card round. White Sox leadoff man Sam Antonacci helped keep the attack churning with a three-hit game, and fellow rookie Braden Montgomery added two hits and two runs. Montgomery has three straight multi-hit games and four overall during a six-game hitting streak in which he is 11-for-23 (.478). Murakami's first multi-homer game since July 26, meanwhile, gave him a club-high 35 home runs. "Right now, being at-bat, I'm feeling great, feeling comfortable out there," Murakami said through an interpreter. "So I'm doing really good." On the bad side, Chicago shortstop Colson Montgomery on Friday broke Mark Reynolds' single-season MLB record for strikeouts. Montgomery has 224; Reynolds had 223 with Arizona in 2009. Colorado (57-103) managed just four hits in losing its fifth straight game. TJ Rumfield smacked a solo home run as part of a two-hit night, and Ezequiel Tovar doubled. The Rockies, who have the worst record in the majors, will turn to left-hander Jose Quintana as he tries to play havoc on his former team's bid for a division crown. Quintana (2-3, 5.40 ERA) has made just 10 starts in his first season with Colorado amid injuries to his right hamstring and left elbow. "I think he would have had a good year if he would have stayed healthy," Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said. Quintana was a mainstay in the White Sox rotation from 2012 until he was traded in the middle of the 2017 season, going 50-54 with a 3.51 ERA in 172 appearances (169 starts). Facing the visiting Seattle Mariners last Saturday, Quintana took a no-decision in a 5-3 win after permitting three runs and five hits in four innings. He walked one and struck out two while throwing 70 pitches in his first appearance since May 24. Quintana is 1-2 with a 4.24 ERA in four appearances and three starts vs. the White Sox, with 19 strikeouts in 17 innings. Right-hander Davis Martin will start for the White Sox on Saturday as he faces the Rockies for the first time. While he remains in search of his first victory since June 10, Martin (9-7, 3.84 ERA) has pitched effectively down the stretch. He's 0-1 with an 0.89 ERA in four September starts covering 20 1/3 innings. Martin is coming off a no-decision on Sunday against Detroit. He allowed three hits over 4 1/3 scoreless innings with two walks and a hit batter in Chicago's 8-1 win. Martin's six strikeouts were his most since July 29. --Field Level Media

item.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo threatens Mexico’s coast, landfall expected Monday
item.description: Hurricane Polo moved away from Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday after it regained the highest Category 5 strength, before an expected return to make landfall in Baja California Sur on Monday, forecasters said.
item.dc:creator: Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Polo moved away from Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday after it regained the highest Category 5 strength, before an expected return to make landfall in Baja California Sur on Monday, forecasters said. On Saturday morning, Polo was about 425 miles south west of the Mexican resort town of Cabo Corrientes, with maximum sustained winds of 160 mph, according to the US National Hurricane Center. The storm was moving north west at 10 mph. AccuWeather, a private forecaster, reported that 24 hours after hitting Baja California, the hurricane was expected to make a second landfall along the coast of mainland northwestern Mexico, bringing potential life-threatening flash flooding to parts of Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Sonora and Chihuahua. The hurricane’s heavy rain and strong winds along Mexico’s Pacific coast forced evacuations, port closures and school cancellations this week. In the resort city of San Jose del Cabo, police officers restricted access to a beach on Friday as the hurricane generated high waves and dangerous surf conditions. Hurricane conditions are possible on Monday afternoon from Punta Eugenia to Santa Fe in Baja California, the NHC said. Polo is expected to dump 4 to 8 inches of rain across parts of Baja California Sur, with maximum amounts of 10 inches, which could produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, the NHC said. It could also cause life-threatening surf, rip currents and coastal flooding.

item.title: Bangladesh launches measles vaccination drive amid deadly outbreak
item.description: Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday, targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday, targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever [USN:L4N44Z0Q9 TEXT:"measles outbreak"], which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands. The month-long campaign aims to vaccinate children aged 6 months to 59 months who missed earlier immunisation efforts after authorities lowered the minimum vaccination age from the usual 9 months because of the outbreak. The outbreak has exposed gaps in childhood immunisation and put growing pressure on health services, already grappling with a seasonal surge in [USN:L4N44Y01W TEXT:"dengue"] infections. Bangladesh is currently experiencing the world's largest measles outbreak, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It has recorded 1,087 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths, including 101 laboratory-confirmed fatalities. Since March 15, authorities have reported nearly 187,000 suspected cases and 21,099 confirmed infections, with more than 165,000 people hospitalised, health ministry data showed. Health experts attributed the crisis to disruptions in routine immunisation programmes in 2024 and 2025, when political turmoil, changes to vaccine procurement and the postponement or cancellation of vaccination campaigns left many children unprotected. Missed vaccinations and vaccine supply disruptions left children vulnerable to infection, particularly infants under 9 months who are too young to receive routine measles immunisation, helping fuel transmission across age groups. Since April, Bangladesh has [USN:L1N40O03M TEXT:"vaccinated"] nearly 20 million children through emergency and follow-up campaigns. However, experts say significant immunity gaps remain, with many eligible children still unvaccinated or missed during previous drives. They say reaching every eligible child in the latest campaign will be critical to slowing transmission and preventing future outbreaks of the highly contagious disease. Authorities said the campaign will help close immunity gaps, reduce severe illness and deaths, and break chains of transmission across Bangladesh.

item.title: Dodgers LHP Blake Snell tests playoff readiness against Giants
item.description: Left-hander Blake Snell will get an opportunity to prove he's healthy and deserving of a spot in the postseason rotation when he starts for the Los Angeles Dodgers as a three-game road series against the San Francisco Giants continues on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Left-hander Blake Snell will get an opportunity to prove he's healthy and deserving of a spot in the postseason rotation when he starts for the Los Angeles Dodgers as a three-game road series against the San Francisco Giants continues on Saturday afternoon. With the National League West title assured, the No. 2 seed in the NL playoffs locked up, and a first-round bye secured, the Dodgers got a brilliant pitching performance from imported ace Tarik Skubal in a 2-0 win in the series opener Friday. Coming off his worst outing with the Dodgers, having allowed four runs over five innings in a 10-4 loss to the Giants in Los Angeles last week, Skubal demonstrated his readiness for Game 1 of the National League Division Series next week by striking out 10 in seven shutout innings on Friday. Skubal is 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA since the Dodgers acquired him from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline last month. The Dodgers (98-62) would love to see something similar from Snell (4-1, 1.86 ERA), the oft-injured left-hander who pulled himself from his most recent start after one inning on Sept. 16 because of tightness in his left groin. Concerned that he might need an MRI or some time off, the Dodgers were comforted in watching the veteran throw a bullpen session the next day, allowing him to remain on schedule for Saturday's dress rehearsal for a front-line spot in LA's bid for a third consecutive World Series title. Snell, who said his goal had been to get through five innings last week in Cincinnati despite feeling a twinge in his groin while warming up, said afterward that having experience with injuries led to a personal decision that might have saved his season. "I strained it four different times," he told reporters about his painful career. "For me to stop, that's a first. That was definitely the right move." The start in San Francisco will be his first since he pitched one season for the Giants in 2024. In fact, he hasn't faced his old mates anywhere since joining the Dodgers last year, retaining a 5-1 record and 1.61 ERA in nine career starts against them. The 33-year-old has a winning record at Oracle Park in San Francisco, going 3-2 with a 2.48 ERA in 15 starts. Eleven starts came in 2024, when he went 1-2 with a 2.85 ERA in 11 home outings. The Giants (65-95) will counter with a left-hander, rookie Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 3.65 ERA), who threw five shutout innings, allowing three hits, and didn't get a decision in a 3-1 road loss to the Dodgers on Sunday. It was his first outing against Los Angeles. Having pitched in relief in his two previous appearances before the gem at Dodger Stadium, the 23-year-old brings a streak of 10 shutout innings into the game, having limited opponents to five hits without issuing a walk. He struck out 10 in those 10 innings. Giants manager Tony Vitello would take a repeat of Friday's pitching performance in the rematch. Starter Yunior Marte and relievers Sam Hentges, Joel Kuhnel, Dylan Smith and Tristan Beck combined to limit LA to seven hits, but San Francisco still has lost three games in a row. "The best way to win is to throw the first punch (offensively)," Vitello told reporters after the game. "We weren't able to do that, but maybe with the way those guys pitched, (the offense) can support the effort the next two days." --Field Level Media

item.title: Au Brésil, le coût élevé de la vie compromet la candidature de Lula à sa réélection
item.description: Depuis la boucherie où il travaille, près du centre historique de São Paulo, Kleyton Zacarioto explique que la fréquentation diminue depuis des années, selon lui du fait d'une longue période de hausse des prix de la nourriture.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Depuis la boucherie où il travaille, près du centre historique de São Paulo, Kleyton Zacarioto explique que la fréquentation diminue depuis des années, selon lui du fait d'une longue période de hausse des prix de la nourriture. La pression prolongée sur le budget des ménages a détourné cet homme de 39 ans de la candidature du président de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui brigue un quatrième mandat lors des élections du mois prochain. Kleyton Zacarioto affirme que Lula est le seul candidat pour lequel il est certain de ne pas voter, même s’il reconnaît que le président « a fait de bonnes choses » lors de son premier mandat dans les années 2000. « Quelqu’un qui touche le salaire minimum n’a aucun moyen de s’en sortir », a-t-il déclaré. Âgé de 80 ans, Lula demande aux électeurs de faire preuve de patience, tout en mettant en avant un taux de chômage historiquement bas, une réduction des inégalités et un ralentissement de l’inflation ces derniers mois pour affirmer que la situation économique est meilleure qu’il n’y paraît. Mais la frustration de Kleyton Zacarioto reflète un défi qui mine les têtes de liste partout dans le monde depuis la pandémie : convaincre les électeurs que l’amélioration des indicateurs économiques a de l’importance alors que beaucoup se sentent encore pris à la gorge par des années de hausse des prix. PROMESSES ELECTORALES « Je sais que la situation n’est pas encore idéale, mais je vous garantis que l’inflation restera sous contrôle », a promis Lula dans un récent spot de campagne, affirmant qu’il savait ce que c’était que de ne pas joindre les deux bouts. Depuis des mois, les sondages indiquent un coude à coude entre Lula et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l’ancien président d'extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro, écarté de la course après avoir été condamné pour tentative de coup d’État. Les sondages suggèrent que la situation économique est l’une des principales raisons pour lesquelles Lula peine à se démarquer du sénateur Bolsonaro. Près de la moitié des Brésiliens estiment que la situation économique s’est détériorée au cours de l’année écoulée, selon un sondage Quaest publié en septembre, contre seulement 19% considérant qu’elle s’est améliorée. Le sénateur Bolsonaro a fait du pouvoir d’achat un thème central de sa campagne, comparant fréquemment les prix actuels dans les supermarchés à ceux pratiqués sous la présidence de son père. La campagne de Lula a riposté en lançant un site web baptisé « Marché des mensonges » pour contester ces allégations. Elle a également déposé une plainte auprès de la Cour électorale supérieure, qui supervise les élections au Brésil, accusant la campagne du sénateur de mentir sur les prix. LA « VIBECESSION » FRAPPE LE BRÉSIL Selon certains experts, ce débat sur le coût de la vie reflète le décalage entre, d'une part, l’amélioration des indicateurs du marché du travail et de l’inflation, et d'autre part la réalité quotidienne de nombreux ménages. « Tous les grands chiffres indiquent que ce gouvernement a fait du bon travail », a déclaré Thomas Traumann, analyste politique et auteur. « Le fait est qu'au quotidien, les gens ne sont tout simplement pas d’accord avec cela. » L'analyste a établi un parallèle avec les difficultés rencontrées par le président américain Joe Biden en 2024 pour combler le fossé entre les données macroéconomiques positives et le sentiment négatif des consommateurs, un phénomène que la commentatrice économique Kyla Scanlon a surnommé la « vibecession ». « Le gouvernement peut se prévaloir de réalisations, mais les électeurs se demandent dans quelle mesure ces progrès se sont répercutés sur leur propre situation familiale », a déclaré Felipe Nunes, fondateur et PDG de l’institut de sondage Quaest. « Les électeurs jugent l’économie à l’aune de leur capacité à payer leurs factures, à consommer des biens et des services, et à atteindre leurs objectifs personnels », a-t-il ajouté. Les prix des denrées alimentaires et l’alourdissement de la dette expliquent en partie pourquoi de nombreuses familles n’ont constaté qu’une faible amélioration de leur pouvoir d’achat depuis la fin de la pandémie. Si l’inflation alimentaire a fortement ralenti — et les prix ont même baissé entre juin et août —, des années de hausses de prix vertigineuses continuent de peser sur le budget des ménages, les prix restant bien au-dessus des niveaux d’avant la pandémie. Dans le même temps, le service de la dette des ménages, hors crédits immobiliers, a atteint le niveau record de 26,6 % des revenus en juin, selon les données de la banque centrale, alors que les fintechs en pleine expansion proposaient des crédits faciles à des taux d’intérêt élevés et que l’essor des paris en ligne absorbait des milliards de reais de revenus des ménages, plongeant de nombreuses familles dans des difficultés financières. Ce fardeau a été aggravé par le taux d’intérêt de référence brésilien de 13,75%, l’un des taux réels les plus élevés au monde, que la banque centrale a progressivement commencé à abaisser tout en surveillant de près l’inflation. DES ÉLECTEURS SCEPTIQUES Lula a tenté de réagir. À deux semaines du premier tour, il a dévoilé des mesures qui semblaient viser à augmenter le revenu disponible, notamment une augmentation de 15% d’un programme social phare qui entrera en vigueur avant le second tour des élections fin octobre. Il a également annoncé un décret interdisant les paris en ligne à compter du 6 octobre. Mais les sondages suggèrent que ces mesures n’ont pas encore eu d’impact significatif sur l’opinion des électeurs. Le sénateur Bolsonaro fait quant à lui campagne en promettant une baisse du coût des denrées alimentaires grâce à des réductions d’impôts, de meilleures liaisons de transport, l’extension des capacités de stockage des céréales et une augmentation de la production nationale d’engrais. Lula met en avant la croissance de la production agricole, les stocks alimentaires de l’État et l’élargissement du crédit rural. Mais ces propositions n’ont pas encore trouvé d’écho auprès de nombreux Brésiliens. Conceição Melquiades, venue de Manaus pour faire ses courses au marché et qui peine à faire face à la hausse des prix de l’électricité et des produits alimentaires, a déclaré qu’elle n’avait vu aucune « véritable proposition » de la part des candidats. « Au final, ça ne changera pas grand-chose », a-t-elle estimé.

item.title: En Brasil, la frustración por el costo de la vida socava las posibilidades de reelección de Lula
item.description: Desde la carnicería en la que trabaja, cerca del centro histórico de São Paulo, Kleyton Zacarioto afirma que la afluencia de clientes lleva años disminuyendo debido, según él, a un largo periodo de subida de los precios de los alimentos.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Lais Morais, Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: Desde la carnicería en la que trabaja, cerca del centro histórico de São Paulo, Kleyton Zacarioto afirma que la afluencia de clientes lleva años disminuyendo debido, según él, a un largo periodo de subida de los precios de los alimentos. La prolongada presión sobre los presupuestos familiares ha llevado a este hombre de 39 años a oponerse a la candidatura del presidente de izquierda, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, para un cuarto mandato en las elecciones del próximo mes. Zacarioto afirma que Lula es el único candidato al que sabe que no votará, aunque reconoce que el presidente "hizo cosas buenas" durante su primer mandato, en la década de 2000. "Alguien que gana el salario mínimo no tiene forma de salir adelante", afirmó. Lula, de 80 años, pide paciencia a los votantes, al tiempo que destaca el desempleo en mínimos históricos, la reducción de la desigualdad y la moderación de la inflación en los últimos meses para argumentar que la economía está mejor de lo que parece. Pero la frustración de Zacarioto refleja un reto que ha acosado a los gobernantes de todo el mundo desde la pandemia: convencer a los votantes de que la mejora de los indicadores económicos es importante, cuando muchos siguen sintiéndose agobiados por años de precios elevados. "Sé que la situación aún no es ideal, pero garantizo que la inflación se mantendrá bajo control", prometió Lula en un reciente anuncio de campaña, afirmando que sabía lo que era no llegar a fin de mes. Desde hace meses, las encuestas muestran un empate técnico entre Lula y el senador Flavio Bolsonaro, hijo del expresidente de derecha Jair Bolsonaro, a quien se le prohibió presentarse tras ser condenado por un intento de golpe de Estado. Las encuestas sugieren que la economía es una de las principales razones por las que a Lula le ha costado tanto mantenerse por delante del senador Bolsonaro. Casi la mitad de los brasileños afirma que la economía ha empeorado en el último año, según una encuesta de Quaest publicada en septiembre, frente a solo un 19% que afirma que la economía ha mejorado. El senador Bolsonaro ha convertido en eje central de su campaña la preocupación de que los sueldos ya no dan para lo mismo que antes, contrastando con frecuencia los precios actuales en los supermercados con los de la época de la presidencia de su padre. La campaña de Lula ha contraatacado con una página web denominada "Mercado de las mentiras" para rebatir estas afirmaciones. Además, ha presentado una denuncia ante el Tribunal Superior Electoral, que supervisa las elecciones en Brasil, acusando a la campaña del senador de mentir sobre los precios. LA "VIBECESSION" LLEGA A BRASIL Los expertos afirman que el debate sobre el costo de la vida refleja una brecha entre las mejoras en las medidas laborales y contra la inflación y lo que muchos hogares viven en su día a día. "Todas las grandes cifras indican que este ha sido un buen gobierno", afirmó Thomas Traumann, analista político y autor. "El hecho es que la gente de a pie simplemente no está de acuerdo con eso". Traumann estableció comparaciones con las dificultades que afrontó el presidente de Estados Unidos, Joe Biden, en 2024 para superar la desconexión que perciben los votantes entre los datos macroeconómicos positivos y el sentimiento negativo de los consumidores, un fenómeno para el que la comentarista económica Kyla Scanlon acuñó el neologismo "vibecession". "El Gobierno tiene logros que puede destacar, pero los votantes se preguntan en qué medida esos avances han llegado a sus propios hogares", señaló Felipe Nunes, fundador y director ejecutivo de la empresa de sondeos Quaest. "Los votantes juzgan la economía en función de su capacidad para pagar las facturas, consumir bienes y servicios, y alcanzar sus objetivos personales". Los precios de los alimentos y la creciente carga de la deuda ayudan a explicar por qué muchas familias apenas han notado una mejora en su poder adquisitivo tras la pandemia. Aunque la inflación de los alimentos se ha frenado considerablemente —e incluso los precios bajaron entre junio y agosto—, años de fuertes subidas de precios siguen ejerciendo presión sobre los presupuestos familiares, ya que los precios se mantienen muy por encima de los niveles previos a la pandemia. Al mismo tiempo, el servicio de la deuda de los hogares, excluidas las hipotecas, alcanzó un récord del 26,6% de los ingresos en junio, según datos del banco central, ya que las empresas fintech en rápido crecimiento ofrecían crédito fácil a tasas de interés elevadas y el auge de las apuestas en línea absorbió miles de millones de reales de los ingresos de los hogares, lo que llevó a muchas familias a una situación de dificultades financieras. Esta carga se ha visto agravada por la tasa de interés de referencia de Brasil, del 13,75%, una de las tasas reales más altas del mundo, que el Banco Central ha comenzado a reducir gradualmente sin perder de vista la inflación. "Si se analizan los datos del mercado laboral, los indicadores de pobreza y la expansión de la clase media, se observa un panorama de avances significativos en los últimos años", afirmó Marcelo Neri, economista de la Fundación Getulio Vargas. "Pero cuando se tienen en cuenta la inflación acumulada de los alimentos, las tasas de interés y las apuestas en línea, el resultado es, digamos, un empate con muchos goles marcados por ambos bandos". VOTANTES ESCÉPTICOS Lula ha intentado reaccionar. A dos semanas de la primera vuelta, Lula presentó [USN:S0N44O03Q TEXT:"medidas"] que parecían destinadas a aumentar la renta disponible, incluido un incremento del 15% en un programa de bienestar social emblemático, que entrará en vigor antes de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones a finales de octubre. También anunció un decreto que prohíbe las apuestas en línea a partir del 6 de octubre. Pero las encuestas sugieren que las medidas aún no han tenido un impacto significativo en la opinión de los votantes. Volviendo al mercado, Carlos Alves da Silva lleva 15 años en el puesto de frutas y verduras Barraca do Juca, cuyas paredes están empapeladas con carteles de la telenovela de los años noventa que se rodó allí. Afirma que no sobrevivirá hasta 2028 si gana Lula. "Es solo cuestión de endeudarse y luchar por saldar la deuda al mes siguiente", afirma Alves, que apoya al senador Bolsonaro. Los candidatos han intentado trazar un camino a seguir. El senador Bolsonaro basa su campaña en la reducción de los costos de los alimentos mediante recortes fiscales, mejores conexiones de transporte, la ampliación del almacenamiento de cereales y una mayor producción nacional de fertilizantes. Lula apuesta por el aumento de la producción agrícola, las reservas gubernamentales de alimentos y la ampliación del crédito rural. Pero esas propuestas aún no han calado entre muchos brasileños. Conceição Melquiades, una visitante del mercado procedente de Manaus que tiene dificultades para hacer frente al aumento de los precios de la electricidad y los alimentos, afirmó que no ha visto ninguna "propuesta real" por parte de los candidatos. "Al final, no va a cambiar gran cosa".

item.title: Tigers' Justin Verlander to make final career start in matchup vs. Pirates
item.description: Justin Verlander's last career appearance will come at the perfect place: Detroit.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Justin Verlander's last career appearance will come at the perfect place: Detroit. The rest of his final season didn't go as planned. The future Hall of Famer will start for the Tigers on Saturday afternoon against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Verlander, who announced this past summer that he would retire after the season, will make just his second start of the year. Detroit (75-85) lost six of its previous eight games before posting an 8-7 victory over Pittsburgh (81-79) on Friday. Verlander's second stint with the Tigers was supposed to be a season-long extravaganza as a member of the rotation. Injuries prevented that from happening after the 43-year-old right-hander made a road start against Arizona on March 30, giving up five runs and six hits over 3 2/3 innings in a 9-6 loss. "I honestly didn't envision this being my last season, but that's the way things go," Verlander said. "(I) slowly came to that realization through the course of the year when I just couldn't get back out there, so that's been quite difficult. But I've come to terms with it and feel good about where things are at, and I've been so thankful." Verlander (0-1, 12.27 ERA) will make his first start at home in a Tigers uniform since Aug. 20, 2017. He's not expected to go deep into the game. "There's no script," he said. "Everybody feels comfortable with 20 pitches, and then after that, we're kind of in a 'who knows?'" Verlander battled a hamstring injury in recent months, suffered during his rehab from a hip injury. "I skipped about a month's worth of rehab to be able to do this," he said. "Never has it been, 'Make one simulated inning and go ahead.' But that's the only way we can make it work." Verlander pitched for the Tigers from 2005-17 until he was dealt to World Series champion Houston in 2017. He'll make the 557th and final start of his career on Saturday, and he said he's more nervous for this outing than for most of his previous ones. "I haven't really known what to expect this whole time coming into this weekend. And yesterday and today, particularly today, I started really noticing, like, I'm really on edge right now and I have a lot of angst in a good way," Verlander said on Friday. "I enjoy it, but I was like, 'Oh wow, this is more than maybe I anticipated.'" Verlander is 5-2 with a 3.08 ERA in 10 career appearances (all starts) vs. Pittsburgh. Even the Pirates have a strong connection to Verlander. Manager Don Kelly was his former teammate in the minor leagues and with the Tigers. "It's unbelievable the career that he's had, no doubt, first-ballot Hall of Famer," Kelly said. "To play third base in his first start in Double-A, and then to have the years that we had from '09 through '14, and then back again in 2019, my first year coaching ... elite competitor. He's a winner, and just the way that he's gone about it and the success that he's had, it'll be cool to be there for his last start on Saturday." Kelly said he expects his ex-teammate to go out with a bang. "He's a competitor, man, and he wants to be out there," Kelly said. "I think the thing that stood out with Justin is you may have beat him, but he never lost. He just kept on going, and that's just the mindset that he took: He was always going to go out there and keep competing, and this year was no different." Pittsburgh will turn to right-hander Kirby Yates (2-5, 3.32 ERA) to start Saturday's game. Yates allowed one hit in a scoreless inning in his last outing, a no-decision against the St. Louis Cardinals on Wednesday. He also pitched a scoreless inning against Detroit on Aug. 17. Yates is 2-1 with a 3.57 ERA in 18 career relief appearances vs. the Tigers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Italy's Catania airport shuts as Etna ash halts flights
item.description: Flights at Italy's Catania airport were suspended on Saturday due to volcanic ash from Mount Etna's ongoing activity and weather conditions, the company operating the Sicilian hub said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Flights at Italy's Catania airport were suspended on Saturday due to volcanic ash from Mount Etna's ongoing activity and weather conditions, the company operating the Sicilian hub said. All arrivals at the airport, Italy's fifth-busiest by passenger traffic, have been suspended until 1000 GMT on Sunday. Mount Etna, Europe's highest and most active volcano, frequently disrupts flights at Catania, but ash emissions have been [USN:L8N4560VH TEXT:"particularly intense this summer"], affecting thousands of travellers during the peak holiday season.

item.description: Fay, situada cerca de las Azores, se debilitó de nuevo hasta convertirse en una depresión tropical, según informó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos en su último boletín emitido el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fay, situada cerca de las Azores, se debilitó de nuevo hasta convertirse en una depresión tropical, según informó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos en su último boletín emitido el sábado.
